diocese: The Episcopal Diocese of South Carolina
notes: Source is a single-column, one-week-per-Sunday layout (confirmed by rendering and visually comparing pages 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 against the linearized `pdftotext -layout` extraction before trusting it) -- no multi-column interleaving risk was found.

The source's own introduction states: "The Anglican Cycle of Prayer is noted in blue. Visitations by the bishop have been noted on the calendar in green. On other Sundays, we pray for other congregations and institutions of the diocese, along with other ministries." Every week in the source prints two items: (1) the diocese's own local subject (a congregation or diocesan institution/ministry/office), and (2) that week's entry from the worldwide Anglican Cycle of Prayer (printed in blue italics). Both are recorded here as this entry's `subjects`, in the order printed (diocesan subject first, Anglican Cycle of Prayer entry second). The Anglican Cycle of Prayer entry is recorded as `type: "category"` rather than `type: "diocese"`/`"province"`, because this schema restricts those two types to scope-'communion' files only; this file's scope is the default 'diocese', so `category` is used instead, exactly as the source's own printed name for that province/church.

A subject printed in green in the source, with "(visitation)" appended after its name/place (marking a bishop's visitation that week), has that parenthetical stripped from `name` and recorded instead as a disclosure in that subject's own `note` field ("Marked as a bishop's visitation in the source (printed in green)."), since it is a status marker rather than part of the congregation's own printed name. It is NOT recorded as `liturgicalNote`, since `liturgicalNote` is reserved for the source's own liturgical/calendar label for the date (e.g. "Palm Sunday"), not a bishop-visitation marker, and this source printed no liturgical Sunday names at all.

Nearly every week's diocesan subject is followed in the source by 1-5 lines naming that congregation's/group's rector, vicar, priest-in-charge, warden(s), or (for a non-parish subject) its chairman/executive director/president -- this schema's subjectShape has no dedicated field for these, so they are preserved verbatim in that subject's own `note` field (each line joined with "; "), rather than being dropped.

Subjects that are an institution rather than a specific worshipping congregation -- a camp/conference center, school, university, or retirement community (e.g. "St. Christopher Camp and Conference Center", "Kanuga Camp and Conference Center, Hendersonville, NC", "Voorhees University", "Porter-Gaud Episcopal School", "Still Hopes Episcopal Retirement Community", "Bishop Gadsden Episcopal Retirement Community", "Sewanee: The University of the South") -- are recorded as `type: "category"`, not `"parish"`, per subjectShape ("category" covers anything "not tied to one congregation"); several of these are outside South Carolina (Kanuga in Hendersonville, NC; Sewanee in Tennessee) but are the diocese's own named subjects for that week, transcribed as printed.

February 15's subject, "St. Philip's Chapel, Denmark, on the campus of Voorhees University", was split into `name`: "St. Philip's Chapel", `place`: "Denmark", with the campus descriptor ("On the campus of Voorhees University.") preserved in that subject's own `note` field, since `place` per this schema is meant to hold only the town/city.

November 1's diocesan subject, "Calvary Episcopal Church (visitation)", is printed with no city/town at all -- the only congregation entry in the whole source missing one. Rather than fabricating a place, this subject is recorded as `type: "category"` (which carries no `place`) instead of `"parish"`; the visitation marker and officer names are preserved in its `note` field, and this judgment call is disclosed there as well.

"The Episcopal Church of the Good Shepherd" is printed as the diocesan subject on two different, non-adjacent weeks for two different towns -- June 7 (Sumter) and September 20 (Summerville) -- transcribed as printed both times; this is the source's own content (two distinct congregations sharing a name), not a duplicate entry or a transcription error.

"The Rev. Shawn Griffth, Associate Chaplain" (November 22) preserves the source's own apparent typo ("Griffth" for "Griffith") verbatim, per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a diocese's own published document.
November 8's subject line reads "Interim Rector" with no person's name given (unlike every other officer line in the source, which names an individual) -- preserved exactly as printed.

The Anglican Cycle of Prayer entries begin repeating partway through the year (e.g. October 25's "The Church of the Province of Central Africa" matches January 4's; November 1 through December 27 each repeat an entry from January 4 through March 8) -- this is the source's own printed content on each date, not a transcription error or an intentional loop constructed here.

The diocese's own cover page gives its short title as "The Diocese of South Carolina", but its body text refers to itself repeatedly and more formally as "The Episcopal Diocese of South Carolina" (e.g. in the January 18, April 12, July 12, October 25 and December 27 entries) -- this fuller form is used for this file's `diocese` field, consistent with this corpus's naming convention for other TEC dioceses' files.

This diocese (The Episcopal Diocese of South Carolina) is distinct from the Episcopal Diocese of Upper South Carolina, a separate diocese not yet held in this corpus; `dioceseShort` is set to "south-carolina" accordingly.
